title: A 2 or 3 room apartment: how to choose right
seoTitle: A 2 or 3 room apartment: how to choose right
description: A 2 or 3 room apartment, how to choose: couple versus family, budget, real area and resale. A concrete guide, with an example at Ilioara Residence.
descriptionLlm: A decision guide, 2 versus 3 rooms at Ilioara Residence (Titan-Dristor, Sector 3, Bucharest). 2 room apartments 107,500-136,500 EUR + VAT, 3 room apartments 151,000-168,000 EUR + VAT, total areas 47-85 sqm, completion December 2026.

lead: Most people get the extra room wrong. Not because they need it, but because they are afraid they might need it somehow, someday. That is how you buy 15 sqm that you dust for two years before you put anything in them. The real question is not "can I afford 3 rooms", it is "what do I do with that space every day". The answer differs enormously between a couple and a family with one child, and the price difference is not small. Below, the decision as it really is, with a concrete example from a building where you can see in black and white what each option costs.

sections.h2: The extra room is not bought out of fear

blocks.x: The classic logic goes like this: I take 3 rooms so I am covered. A child comes, the mother in law comes, I set up an office. These are real scenarios, but most of them stay scenarios. Until then you pay for, heat and furnish a room you use at the capacity of a luxury storage cupboard.

The verdict is simple: the extra room is justified by a need you have now or one you can clearly see in the next two or three years, not by a "what if". If you work from home every day, you need it. If you often have guests who stay the night, you need it. If your answer is "it would be nice to have", that is not a need, it is expensive decoration.

sections.h2: A couple with no children: 2 rooms, almost always

blocks.x: A couple with no children lives, in practice, in a living room with an open kitchen and a bedroom. That is all they use, whatever plans they have on paper. For two adults the third room becomes either a store room, or an office used a few hours a week, or the room you walk into once a month to check that it exists.

The honest exception: two people who both work from home, with calls that overlap. Then the second work room really does count, because otherwise you argue over the only desk. Otherwise, a well laid out 2 room apartment beats a badly used 3 room one. Less to clean, less to heat, and the money left over stays in your pocket.

sections.h2: A family with a child: here 3 rooms are worth the money

blocks.x: The moment the extra room stops being a luxury is the child. A child needs their own space before you realise it, and moving from 2 rooms to 3 in three years means another move, another agent, another set of costs you pay twice.

If you are already a parent, or the plan to become one sits in the window of the next few years, 3 rooms is no longer over buying, it is exactly the right size. Here the price difference turns from an expense into an investment in something you will actually use every day. The rest of the arguments, an office, guests, are a bonus on top of the real need.

sections.h2: The area you use, not the one you pay for

blocks.x: The number of rooms fools you. A generous 2 room apartment, well divided, gives you more lived space than a cramped 3 room one with walls put in badly. What counts is how many square metres actually end up under your feet, not how many doors you count.

At Ilioara Residence the total areas run from 49 to 86 sqm, with a modular layout. That is the important part: the space can adapt. You start with an open layout and close it up later, or the other way round, depending on how life at home changes. You buy square metres you shape around yourself, not a fixed scheme you have to force yourself into.

sections.h2: The price difference, in real money

blocks.x: The theory is fine until you see the figures. At Ilioara Residence, in the Titan-Dristor area of Sector 3, a 2 room apartment is between 107,500 and 136,500 EUR + VAT. A 3 room one, between 151,000 and 168,000 EUR + VAT. We are talking about tens of thousands of euros of difference, money that, for a couple, would sit better in a parking space, a premium renovation or simply not put on the table at all.

The structure of the building says a lot about who the typical buyer is: ground floor plus 8 storeys: at the top, 2 penthouses already sold, and the rest 31 apartments, 4 per floor, of which 1 with 3 rooms and 3 with 2 rooms. That ratio is not an accident. It reflects exactly the real demand, more people need 2 rooms than 3. The lower floors have almost sold out, and what is left, most of it, is up on 6 and 7, the part with the best view. Out of 31, 12 are still available.

sections.h2: Resale and letting: 2 rooms move more easily, but not always

blocks.x: When you think you might sell or let one day, the general rule is that 2 room apartments move more easily and more quickly. The pool of buyers and tenants is bigger, because a 2 room apartment catches the couple, the single person on a budget and the investor. More liquidity, less waiting.

But do not turn that into dogma. In an area with families, near schools and parks, a good 3 room apartment has its own public and holds its value well. Here the location decides. Ilioara is 5 minutes on foot from Nicolae Grigorescu metro station, with trams and a bus a few minutes away, Mega Image and the market at 6-7 minutes, IOR Park at 9. The kind of address that works in both scenarios, sold and let, whatever the number of rooms.

You are a couple with no children in the near window, you want a smaller monthly outlay and liquidity at resale: 2 rooms, no regrets. You are a family, you have a child or one is on the way, you work from home seriously or you want the space so you do not have to move again in three years: 3 rooms, worth the money.

The rest of the details count as much as the number of doors: underfloor heating everywhere, including on the balcony, triple glazed Salamander joinery with 7 chambers, an Ariston boiler of your own, all included in the price. The sale is direct, from the developer, 0% commission for the buyer, and the displayed price is the price, with no surprises at the end. faq.q: What does a 2 room apartment cost compared with a 3 room one at Ilioara Residence?

faq.q: We are a couple with no children. Do we really need 3 rooms?
faq.a: Almost never. In practice a couple uses the living room and one bedroom. The third room ends up a store room or an office used a few hours a week. The real exception is when you both work from home every day, with calls that overlap.

faq.q: How many square metres do the apartments have and how are they divided?
faq.a: The total areas run from 49 to 86 sqm, with a modular layout, meaning the space can adapt. What counts is the metres you actually use, not just the number of rooms.

faq.q: Which is easier to resell and to let, 2 or 3 rooms?
faq.a: As a rule 2 room apartments move faster, because they have a bigger pool of buyers and tenants. In an area with families, near schools and parks, a good 3 room apartment holds its value too. The location decides.

faq.q: What is included in the price of the apartments?
faq.a: Underfloor heating everywhere, including on the balcony, triple glazed Salamander joinery with 7 chambers and a 24 kW Ariston boiler of your own, all included. Parking is taken separately: a Klauss double space 25,000 EUR + VAT, a single one 20,000 EUR + VAT.

faq.q: How many apartments are still available and on which floors?
faq.a: Out of 33 apartments, 12 are still available. The lower floors have almost sold out, and most of those left are up on floors 6 and 7, the part with the best view. Completion in December 2026.
